# The Taazaa templates, and what replaces them

The Taazaa documentation skill's Mermaid diagrams share five defects: one layered shape forced
on every system, unlabelled arrows, levels mixed in one picture, no boundary, legend or element
types, and nothing tying a box to code. Cairn does not edit that repository; it owns its own
standard (`docs/diagram-standard/`) and the Taazaa diagrams were transcribed into the
description format only so the defects could be counted.

The transcriptions are in [`taazaa-original/`](taazaa-original/). Running the checker over them
gives the numbers below, and every replacement in `examples/` passes with none.

## The transcriptions, measured

| Transcription | Violations | Rules it breaks |
|---|---|---|
| [`architecture.yaml`](taazaa-original/architecture.yaml) | 47 | R1, R3, R4, R7, R9, R13 |
| [`data-flow.yaml`](taazaa-original/data-flow.yaml) | 53 | R1, R2, R3, R4, R7, R13 |

## The five defects

**One layered shape forced on every system.** `taazaa-original/architecture.yaml`: five boundaries named Client Layer, API Layer, Service Layer, Data Layer and External Services, which say how the picture is drawn rather than what the product owns.

**Unlabelled arrows.** Both transcriptions: every relationship has no 'what', so none says what passes or why.

**Levels mixed in one picture.** `taazaa-original/data-flow.yaml`: processing steps (Validation, Transformation, Computation) drawn as components among the systems they process.

**No boundary, legend or element types.** `taazaa-original/data-flow.yaml` has no boundary at all; neither transcription carries a legend or a one-line responsibility.

**Nothing tying a box to code.** Both transcriptions: no evidence reference anywhere, so no box can be checked against a repository.

## Which template becomes which replacement

| Taazaa template diagram | Replacement | Why it changes |
|---|---|---|
| High-Level Architecture | [examples/01-context-shop](examples/01-context-shop.svg) | two levels instead of one mixed picture |
| High-Level Architecture | [examples/02-containers-shop](examples/02-containers-shop.svg) | a real boundary; every arrow says what and how |
| Communication patterns / service catalog diagram | [examples/02-containers-shop](examples/02-containers-shop.svg) | sync, async and build-time are line styles, not separate drawings |
| High-Level Data Flow, data flow scenarios | [examples/05-flow-place-order](examples/05-flow-place-order.svg) | processing steps belong in a flow, not among systems |
| Sequence: primary workflow, data creation | [examples/05-flow-place-order](examples/05-flow-place-order.svg) | numbered messages with route and evidence |
| Sequence: authentication flow (both copies) | [examples/06-flow-token-auth-cairn](examples/06-flow-token-auth-cairn.svg) | real participants, an alt fragment for success and refusal |
| Data Flow Map with PII Indicators | [examples/04-personal-data-shop](examples/04-personal-data-shop.svg) | a data-class overlay on the container view |
| Security Architecture (zones) | [examples/03-trust-shop](examples/03-trust-shop.svg) | zones only where isolation exists; findings marked inferred |
| Module Architecture Overview, Module Dependencies | [examples/07-components-shop-api](examples/07-components-shop-api.svg) | components of one container, named for what they do |
| Logic / Computation Architecture (domain) | [examples/07-components-shop-api](examples/07-components-shop-api.svg) | same rules |
| Calculation Flow (domain) | [examples/05-flow-place-order](examples/05-flow-place-order.svg) | same rules |
| Entity Relationship Diagram, Rule Data Model | [examples/08-data-model-shop](examples/08-data-model-shop.svg) | fields shown, associations labelled |
| Rule Lifecycle | [examples/09-lifecycle-memory-cairn](examples/09-lifecycle-memory-cairn.svg) | a lifecycle diagram with labelled transitions |
| Configuration Architecture | (removed) | a generated table of settings, defaults and owners; configuration sources are not architecture |

Examples 01 to 05, 07 and 08 describe a four-repository sandbox product ("Shop") used to
test the system model; 06 and 09 describe Cairn's own code. Each `.md` beside an `.svg` in
`examples/` is that diagram's evidence table.
